name: scheduler-update
description: Modify an existing scheduled job by its ID. action=resume brings a suspended (failed) or paused (drift) job back to active; action=pause holds an active job; action=edit changes the job in place. Use edit, not scheduler-create, when asked to change a routine: a new time, reworded instructions, an added recipient. On a recurring job, change the cadence with cron_expr. run_at is for one-shot jobs: on a recurring job it moves only the next run and leaves the cron unchanged, so the reschedule does not stick. Pass task_payload to reword what the job does. Edit overwrites the job's schedule and task. It never adds a run, so a request for an additional run is scheduler-create. Get the job_id from scheduler-list. If more than one active job could be the one meant, ask which, citing each one's time, before editing. Afterwards, say what changed on the existing schedule.

inputs.cron_expr: string? (edit only — new cron expression for a recurring job)
inputs.run_at: timestamp? (edit only — new ISO 8601 run time for a one-shot job)
